config.title: Controlled DatePicker

intro.title: Controlled DatePicker
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a controlled DatePicker component in React. You will learn how to manage a selected date as a state variable and update it based on user input. The core concept is controlled components, where React state serves as the single source of truth for form elements. You will use React's useState hook for state management and the HTML input element with type='date' for the date picker interface. This exercise will help you understand how to handle form inputs in a declarative React way.
intro.usecase: Controlled DatePickers are essential in any form-based application where users need to select dates with precision and validation. You'll find them in travel booking sites for selecting flight dates, in healthcare applications for scheduling appointments, and in financial dashboards for filtering transaction date ranges. As a developer, you'll implement controlled DatePickers when building event registration forms, project management tools with deadline selectors, or analytics platforms with time-based filters. This pattern ensures the selected date is always synchronized with your application state, enabling real-time validation and dynamic UI updates.

objectives: Initialize a state variable to store the selected date in a React component
Bind the state variable to a DatePicker component's value prop
Implement a handler function to update state when the date changes
Configure the DatePicker component to use the handler via its onChange prop
Render a controlled DatePicker that displays and updates the selected date
Manipulate the date state to reset or set a default value programmatically
Integrate the controlled DatePicker into a form with other input elements

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the DatePicker component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named DatePicker that returns null for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure the component name matches exactly.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create your DatePicker component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A DatePicker component is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: The DatePicker component is created as a functional component and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component is named exactly 'DatePicker' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Create a functional component named DatePicker that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize state for the selected date
steps.instruction: Inside your DatePicker component, initialize a state variable named 'selectedDate' using useState. Set its initial value to null.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The pattern is: const [variableName, setVariableName] = useState(initialValue).
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'selectedDate' initialized to null, ready to store the user's selected date.
successCriteria: The DatePicker component contains a useState call that declares 'selectedDate' with an initial value of null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to declare a variable named 'selectedDate' with an initial value of null inside the DatePicker component.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the DatePicker component, use useState to create a state variable called 'selectedDate' and set it to null initially.

steps.title: Define the handleDateChange function
steps.instruction: Inside your DatePicker component, define a function named handleDateChange that takes an event parameter and updates the selectedDate state with the event's target.value.
steps.hint: Create a function that will be called when the date input changes. Use the setSelectedDate function from useState to update the state with the new value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a handleDateChange function that can update the selectedDate state when called with an event.
successCriteria: A function named handleDateChange is defined inside the DatePicker component that calls setSelectedDate with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function is named handleDateChange, takes an event parameter, and calls setSelectedDate with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleDateChange function isn't defined correctly. It should be inside the DatePicker component and update the selectedDate state using setSelectedDate(event.target.value).

steps.title: Add the component's return statement
steps.instruction: Add a return statement to your DatePicker component that returns a JSX fragment containing a label and an input element.
steps.hint: Use the return keyword followed by JSX. Start with a fragment (<>...</>) or a div. Inside, add a label and an input element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns JSX structure with a label and an input element.
successCriteria: The DatePicker component has a return statement that returns JSX containing a label and an input element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your return statement includes both a label and an input element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement is missing or doesn't contain the required JSX elements.

steps.title: Add a label for the date picker
steps.instruction: Inside your DatePicker component's return statement, add a <label> element with the text 'Select a date:' before the input element.
steps.hint: Add a JSX label element with descriptive text to make the date picker accessible.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a label element with the text 'Select a date:' placed before the input element in the return statement.
successCriteria: A <label> element with the text 'Select a date:' is added inside the return statement's <div>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the label text is exactly 'Select a date:' and it's placed before the input element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The label element is missing or incorrect. Add a <label> with the text 'Select a date:' inside the return statement.

steps.title: Add the date input element
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement's div, add an input element with type='date'.
steps.hint: Use the <input> tag with the type attribute set to 'date'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now include a date input field in its rendered output.
successCriteria: An input element with type='date' is added inside the div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the date input element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input element, but make sure its type is set to 'date'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding an input element with type='date' inside the div.

steps.title: Connect the input value to state
steps.instruction: In the date input element, set the value attribute to the selectedDate state variable to make it a controlled component.
steps.hint: Add value={selectedDate} to the input element to bind its value to the state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: binding input value to state
<input type="text" value={inputValue} onChange={handleChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The date input will display the current value from selectedDate state, making it a controlled component.
successCriteria: The input element has a value attribute set to selectedDate.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added value={selectedDate} to the input element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element should have a value attribute bound to the selectedDate state variable.

steps.title: Wire the onChange event to the handler
steps.instruction: Confirm that the input's onChange event is already correctly connected to the handleDateChange function.
steps.hint: Check that the input element has an onChange attribute set to handleDateChange.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: confirming an event handler connection
<input onChange={handleInputChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element's onChange event is properly wired to the handleDateChange handler.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: The connection is partially correct. Ensure the input's onChange attribute is set to handleDateChange.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onChange event is not properly connected. Check that the input element has onChange={handleDateChange}.
